newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea lowers '97 GDP growth forecast to 6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Korea lowers '97 GDP growth forecast to 6.0 pct.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) lowered its 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast to a real 6.0 percent from an earlier projection of 6.4 percent, a BOK statement said on Monday.

A central bank official said the bank had downgraded its earlier economic growth forecast made last November because increases in private consumption and corporate facilities investment would be smaller than expected.
"Our economy is expected to hit its bottom in the second half or by the end of this year, and then it will turn around," the official said by telephone.

But the current-account shortfall in 1997 would be reduced to $17 billion from an earlier projection of $18 billion on improving exports that resulted from a recovery of major exports in world markets.
Last year's current account deficit totalled $23.7 billion.

The central bank attributed slow economic growth in the first half to lacklustre private consumption and fixed investments. Private consumption and fixed investments rose 4.5 percent and 0.5 percent respectively during the period, compared with a 7.5 percent and a 6.6 percent growth a year earlier.

Slowing wage hikes, nationwide strikes over a controversial labour bill and a slew of corporate debt defaults dampened consumption in the first half, the statement said, while uncertainty about an economic recovery chilled corporate investment.
During the first half, the current account deficit rose to $11.2 billion with a $6.5 billion trade shortfall and a $4.7 billion deficit in invisible trade balance.
But the nation's economy would show a healthy rise in the second half in line with improving exports and construction investments, the statement said.
It forecast exports would rise 15 percent from July to December on an improving world economy and the yen's strength. Imports would rise 2-3 percent during the period.
The statement said the trade deficit in the second half would total $1.0 billion against $9.66 billion a year ago.
The central bank revised its full-year trade shortfall forecast on a balance of payment basis to $7.5 billion from an earlier projection of $8.7 billion.
FOB exports would total $140 billlion this year, while CIF imports would amount to $154 billion, the statement said.

It said the recovery of macro-economic indicators in the second half would not result from improvements in the nation's industrial structure but from external factors such as the yen's strength and improving world economy.
The central bank forecast international trade would grow about eight percent during the second half.
The central bank recommended that priority be placed on stability and said anticipation for high economic growth should be controlled.
The bank said domestic companies should make efforts to strengthen their financial status and stabilise their overhead expenses, including wages.
